answer: Timed Attention Ledger. Each identity accrues weight only by sustaining verified task engagement across separate scheduling windows; weight decays between windows, so fresh identities start near zero. To reach useful weight, an attacker must pay real compute and human oversight continuously, while honest agents amortize the same cost over long tenure. A jetty of pending validations gates cross-agent actions. Each new identity also posts a visible plume of gradually released credits, delaying first payout until several dawn cycles of consistent activity pass.
